One assassination attempt on this man was thwarted by Manuela Sáenz. He suffered early military defeats at the hands of forces led by José Tomás Boves, after which he successfully petitioned Haiti for military aid. This victor of the Battle of Junín and organizer of a constitutional convention at Cúcuta relied on commanders such as Francisco de Santander and José Antonio Paez to win the Battle of Boyacá, while his victory at Pichincha was aided by José Antonio Sucre. The author of the Carta de Jamaica and the Cartagena Manifesto, name this Venezuelan revolutionary, the namesake of a nation with capitals at La Paz and Sucre.

The Senate's role in investigating this incident led to the McGrain v. Daugherty decision, and John Kendrick first attracted attention to it. The rapid improvement of a cattle ranch in New Mexico raised suspicion about one of its participants, whom Thomas Walsh investigated. Edwin Denby was acquitted for his involvement in it, which involved approving of loans granted by Edward Doheny in exchange for access to the Elk Hills reserves. Harry Sinclair and Albert Fall were implicated in, what scandal of the Harding administration in which Fall received kickbacks for granting exclusive drilling rights in the namesake Wyoming oilfields?

This man served one term as the governor of New Jersey thirteen years after losing a presidential election on a ticket with George Pendleton. The engineer of an offensive beginning at Fort Monroe, this Union commander at the Battle of Seven Pines prompted the General War Order No. 1, two months after which he began the Peninsular Campaign. Replacing Irving McDowell after the First Battle of Bull Run, Lincoln replaced this general after his failure to capitalize on his victory at Antietam. Name this Democratic presidential candidate in 1864, the overly cautious predecessor to Ulysses S Grant as head of the Union armies.

James Coussey led a constitutional convention in this nation, but was circumvented by a transfer of power to the Congress People's Party. John Kufuor replaced Jerry Rawlings as its president in 2001, and an earlier polity of this name was weakened by the Almoravid occupation of Abu Bakr and eventually succumbed to the Susu rebellion. That empire centered at Kumbi Saleh, however, was located to the north of the present day nation of the same name, which was home to the Ashanti Empire. Name this West African nation whose struggle for independence was led by Kwame Nkrumah and whose capital is Accra.

This document, which invoked the second article of the Conference of Nerat, was signed three weeks after an agreement negotiated by its architect, the Peace of Vervins. Some provisions of its first part were remanded by the Peace of Alés, while most of the fifty-six "secret articles" remained unchanged. Montaubon and La Rochelle were among the cities designated as "places de surete" by this agreement, which took the Parlement of Rouen ten years to approve. Dragonnades became common just before its provisions were revoked by the Edict of Fontainebleau. Signed by Henry IV in 1598, name this edict that granted freedom of religion to Huguenots.

This practice was outlawed in Korea during the Gabo reform of 1894. Nicholas V condoned it by issuing the Dum Diversas, but Paul III restricted its practice to non-Christians in the Sublimus Dei. Prohibited by Article IV of the European Convention on Human Rights, Peter Martin led the movement against it in Canada, forty years before a certain act of 1833 prohibited it in Great Britain, twenty-six years after a similar bill was advanced by William Wilberforce. Name this practice protested against in the U.S. By Elijah Lovejoy, William Lloyd Garrison, and Frederick Douglass that was prohibited by the 13th Amendment.

Rutherford B. Hayes was this man's commander during the Civil War, and he campaigned for Hayes while serving as a lawyer in Canton. This man used the slogan "Prosperity at home, Prestige abroad" to support his own front porch campaign, which helped him to defeat William Jennings Bryan in consecutive elections. At the Pan-American Exhibition in Buffalo, he was shot twice by anarchist Leon Czolgosz. Name this American president who presided over the Spanish-American War, who after his assassination was succeeded by Teddy Roosevelt.

After being captured as a boy in Yunnan, he made a name for himself in the military under Prince Yan, who would go on to overthrow the Jianwen emperor to become the Yongle emperor. This Muslim son of a hajji defeated King Alagonakkara, and the Hongxi emperor later made him a garrison commander in Nanjing. He had earlier visited places like Malacca, Hormuz, Siam, and Ceylon during seven voyages. Name this eunuch admiral and emissary for the Ming Dynasty.

Albert Gallatin was skeptical of this act from the beginning, saying that "government prohibitions do always more mischief than had been calculated." A lesser-known element of it was the requirement that ships post a bond equal to the value of the cargo they carried. This law was revealed to be devastating to American shipping, without forcing the expected change in the Orders in Council. It was repealed just days before Thomas Jefferson left office, to be replaced by the equally ineffective Non-Intercourse Act. Name this 1807 law which forbid Americans from trading with either France or Great Britain.

It was referred to in the initial planning stages as Operation Hummingbird, and was partially in response to a speech given at Marburg University by the Vice-Chancellor. One pretext for it was the homosexuality of some of the leading Storm Troopers, but in actuality it was done to curtail a threat to both the army and the Fuhrer's power. Ernst Rohm, a member of Hitler's inner circle, was shot in his cell after being given the chance to commit suicide. What is the name given to the June 30th purge of the SA's leadership and other opponents of the Nazi party?

After he rose to power, this man was abandoned by the tenentes, and his reign saw the rise of the "integralist" movement. This man called himself the "father of the poor." He staged a coup against Washington Luis after which he established the short-lived constitution of 1934, and he was blamed for the assassination attempt on Carlos Lacerda, which prompted him to commit suicide in 1954. This man's first rule ended with a coup by Gaspar Dutra, and as a part of the "Cohen Plan" he established the Estado Novo. Identify this president and long-time dictator of Brazil.

One of the later rulers of this dynasty was Emperor Xianzong who solidified his reign over the kingdom by debasing the Jeidushi governers. The latter Zhou dynasty established by Empress Wu Zetian briefly interrupted this dynasty, whose capital was at Chang'an which was established by Li Yuan as after the decline of the Sui dynasty. This dynasty also saw a major rebellion by a Turkish Sodigan named An Lushan, and it was followed by the Song dynasty. Identify this Chinese dynasty that is best known for its poets such as Li Po and Du Fu.

This country's history saw the signing of the Bulla Aurea by King Andreas in 1222, and the monk Capistrano helped Janos Hunyadi of this country in the siege of Belgrade. A dynasty established in the early 9th Century in this country was defeated at the Battle of Lechfeld by Otto the Great. The 1848 Revolution in this country saw a list of 12 demands, which included secession from its Eastern Neighbor, though more recently, this country tried to withdraw from the Warsaw Pact in a revolution led by Imre Nagy. Identify this country whose people are known as the Magyars.

The Chicago Times claimed that "The cheeks of every American must tingle with shame" due to the "silly, flat, and dishwatery utterances" contained in it. Though it is not the Preamble to the US constitution, its final edition notably features the phrase "under god" which was missing from the first draft, which is known as the Nicolay Copy. Preceded by a long speech by Edward Everett, it reminds the listeners that the "world will little note [...] what we say here" and asserts that "government of the people, by the people, for the people shall not perish from the earth." identify this speech given on November 19, 1863 by Abraham Lincoln.

This country's early settlement involved wars with the Grebo people. Its first governor was Jehudi Ashmun, and its first black leader was Joseph Jenkins Roberts. Some of the first settlers here arrived on the Mary C. Stevens and were graduates of Lincoln University. Martin Delany and Frederick Douglass sparred over this entity's existence, and recent leaders have included war criminal Charles Taylor, who fled to neighbor Sierra Leone, and Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf. Name this country founded by freed black American slaves, with capital Monrovia.

One of this man's supporters had earlier led an attempt to rescue Anthony Burns, while another, Franklin B. Sanborn, had been a student of Emerson. He was supported by the "Secret Six", which included the former vice president of the American Peace Society, Gerrit Smith, and this man met with other supporters in Canada to form the provisional Chatham Constitution. He was involved in the Pottawatomie Killings during Bleeding Kansas, and he wrote the "Vindication of the Invasion" before leading an expedition that began on his rented farm in Maryland. Identify this man who led a slave revolt in Harper's Fairy.

This event was depicted with several people throwing their hats as the central figure raises his right hand on a platform, while the winds of change blow through the windows at upper left. This agreement was hammered out after discussions by Jean-Sylvan Bailly and Jean-Joseph Mounier. Its signatories promised to remain together until a constitution was drafted, and a week later a meeting of the Estates-General was called by Louis XVI. It was signed after the Menus Plaisirs was locked, leaving the 577 members of the Third Estate without a meeting place. Name this agreement of the French Revolution signed in a recreation area.

During the Fete de la Federation, this man who was then the Bishop of Auten took an oath to the as-yet unwritten constitution. Rumored to have been privy to the kidnapping and execution of the Duke of Enghien, this man proposed a namesake partition plan for Belgium. He once hired actors to portray senators in the hopes that he would be named head of a provisional government after the downfall of Napoleon. His country's lead delegate at the Congress of Vienna and the demander of a quarter million dollar bribe during the XYZ affair, name this French diplomat.

This man's opinion in Abelman v. Booth enjoined Wisconsin from interfering with enforcement of federal law. He opined that state extraditions cannot be ordered by federal courts in Kentucky v. Dennison, while he invoked the doctrine of "political questions," claiming that only the president and congress could rule on the legitimacy of alternate state governments during Dorr's Rebellion in Luther v. Borden. This brother-in-law of Francis Scott Key held against implied rights in contracts in Charles River Bridge. Name this Supreme Court Chief Justice who wrote the infamous Dred Scott decision.

This polity contains the Pirin and most of the Rhodope Mountains, while the Rila range, found in its southwest, contains its highest peak, Mount Musala. A bunch of Eneolithic golden artifacts were found in this country's Varna Necropolis archeological site, while the Golden or Round Basilica in Preslav was built during the reign of its first tsar, Simeon I. The Maritsa River flows through Upper Thrace's largest and this country's second largest city, Plovdiv. The Danube forms most of its northern border with Romania, and its eastern coast is on the Black Sea. Identify this southeastern European country with capital at Sofia.

Despite his veto, Congress passed the Adjusted Service Certificate Law or "Bonus Bill" during his presidency. His vice president would win a Nobel Peace Prize for a plan that partially dealt with capping reparations and evacuating the Ruhr Valley, the Dawes Plan. He gained national fame for putting down a police strike in Boston while serving as Governor of Massachusetts. He chose not to sack his predecessor's cabinet following scandals like Teapot Dome. Identify this soft spoken president sandwiched in between Harding and Hoover.

This man's victory at Heronea was tempered by news that Philip V had succumbed to a common foe and the Aetolian League, and that this man's own brother had died at the Battle of the Metaurus. Fabius earned the epithet "Cunctator" due to his actions against this man, who was unable to receive reinforcements thanks to the Council of One Hundred and Four. Called "Dido's Avenger," he won victories at Trebia, Trasimene, and Cannae but was forced out of the Italian Penninsula to defend against Scipio Africanus, who beat him at Zama. Identify this Carthaginian general, who crossed the Alps with some elephants to fight Rome during the Second Punic War.

This group's ultimate defeat came as a consequence of the 13 Years War, and they were opposed by the Lizard League. Despite fighting the Cumans under Andrew II, they were cast out of Hungary and made their way to the Vistula to help Conrad of Mazovia. They acquired the Order of the Brothers of the Sword in 1237. Originally formed as a hospital for the sick during the Third Crusade by some merchants from Lubek and Bremen, they were famously defeated at the First Battle of Tannenberg. Name this medieval German crusading order.

An obscene message on a jacket protesting the draft for the Vietnam War was the subject of Cohen v. This state, while the concept of "no redeeming social value" was put forth by Warren Burger as judging obscenity in Miller v. This state. Allan Bakke sued the Regents of the state university here due to quotas used in admissions to the medical school at Davis. Also the state where Earl Warren served as governor, identify this Western state, home to the man who appointed William Rehnquist to the court, Richard Nixon.

The eunuch Pothinus temporarily removed this ruler from power, resulting in the Battle of Pelusium. Aulus Gabinius helped assassinate this ruler's sister, Berenice IV, while her younger sister, Arsinoe was paraded through Rome in a triumph. She gave birth to Alexander Helios after an affair with the ex-husband of Fulvia. Following a defeat at the Battle of Actium, this mother of Ptolemy XV committed suicide. Identify this Egyptian ruler, lover of Marc Antony and Caesar.

This man seemed to have intended to adopt the pseudonym Alex J. Hidell, and rose to prominence in Marxist circles after he became head of a pro-Castro organization committee in New Orleans, a few years after a conflict with Edwin Walker stemming from this man's stint in the Marine Corps. The Ramsey Clark panel determined that this man probably killed J. D. Tippit following his most famous act, which was captured by the Zapruder Film and examined by the Warren Commission. Identify this man who hit John Connally as he fired the bullets which killed John F. Kennedy.

Edgar Lee Masters was a business partner of this man, who championed the racially charged cause of Ossian Sweet. This man publicly debated Judge Talley on the efficacy of the death penalty, and came out of retirement to represent Lieutenant Massie in Honolulu in 1932. His arguments acquitted Big Bill Haywood from the charge of murdering Idaho Governor Frank Steunenberg, and in another case, he asked the opposing lawyer whether he believed that Joshua made the sun stand still. Name this lawyer who defended a Tennessee man charged with teaching evolution, John Scopes.

The founder of this empire defeated his rival by shooting him with an arrow fletched with the spur of a rooster. That leader of this empire was born in Niani, and defeated Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina. This empire's power declined in the 15th century after attacks from the Mossi and the Tuareg. Another of its leaders gave away so much gold on his 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca that he caused the price of gold to rise in Cairo. Founded by Sundiata, and famously led by Mansa Musa, name this West African empire that shares its name with a modern country whose capital is Bamako.

Judge Joseph H. Nicholson was key in transporting its original form, which may have began as a letter to Arthur Chambers. A note discussing "Anacreon in heaven" appeared alongside it when it was first popularized, following its author's time on the Minden. Darker phrases referencing blood washing out the "foul footsteps' polution" became ignored as stanzas two, three, and four were dropped from most recitations of this piece. Arising from a clash at Fort McHenry, it was the subject of a congressional resolution in 1931. Name this song by Francis Scott Key, the national anthem of the United States.

This conflict started in Caesarea over a dispute about bird sacrifices. Agrippa II fled his capital with his sister, and the army of Cestius Gallus was decimated at the battle of Beth Horon, although the eventual Roman victory is celebrated on the arch of Titus. The Antonia fortress fell to the Romans shortly before the end of the siege of the capital, which had been begun by Vespasian, although Masada held out until 73 A.D. Identify this war described by Josephus, during which the Second Jerusalem Temple was destroyed by the Romans.

This member of Les Groupe des Griots was among the few leaders to recognize the Biafra region of Nigeria as an independent state, and he was excommunicated from the Catholic Church for expelling most of his country's foreign bishops. He served various posts under President Estimé, and then helped overthrow that man's overthrower, Paul Magloire. While in power, he relied on the support of his brutal private army, the Tontons Macoutes. Which leader of Haiti from 1957-71 was succeeded by his similarly nicknamed son Jean-Claude?

A captured letter, the Wethersfield Intercept, revealed that one of the commanders planned to march south to this battle. The only major advance during it was achieved by Alexander Hamilton, when he captured an enemy redoubt. A British band played "The World Turned Upside Down" at the end of this standoff, and second-in-command Charles O'Hara was directed to surrender to George Washington. Name this 1781 battle at which Lord Cornwallis' army was besieged in Virginia, the last major engagement of the American Revolution.

This man had a close relationship with the Japanese leading up to World War II, noting that Japanese conquests were an example of "colored pride." At the age of 95, he renounced his US citizenship to become a citizen of Ghana, where he died one day before the "I Have A Dream" speech. He served as editor of The Crisis, the magazine of an organization he co-founded with Mary White Owington, the NAACP. Name this man who wrote about The Souls of Black Folk and the "Talented Tenth," an early civil rights activist and rival of Booker T. Washington.

This man convened the second council of Constantinople. The subject of the Secret History of Procopius, he sent his general Mundus to attack Dalmatia, and his reign also saw the reconquest of North Africa and Italy. A large scale plague occurred toward the end of his reign, and he had the Eunuch Narses buy off the Blues shortly before having Mundus and Belisarius massacring the Greens to end the Nika riots. Identify this Byzantine emperor, the husband of Theodora, who constructed the Hagia Sophia and promulgated a famous code of law.

Robert Taylor wrote a work called Vessel of Wrath: The Life and Times of... This historical figure. Her second husband's involvement in the Jaybird-Woodpecker War forced their move to the area she is most associated with. She interpreted a tornado as divine approval for her actions, begun after receiving a message to "Go to Kiowa," and referred to herself as "a bulldog running along at the feet of Jesus." name this founder of the Medicine Lodge branch of the Women's Christian Temperance Union, known for smashing up saloons with a hatchet.

This "wisest fool in Christendom" argued for the divine right of kings as an extension of apostolic succession in The True Law of Free Monarchy. His attempt to marry his son to the Infanta Maria of Spain led to a major religious controversy, and he was the target of the plan by Robert Catesby and Guy Fawkes to blow up Parliament, the Gunpowder Plot. This son of Mary, Queen of Scots was the sixth of his name in Scotland, and he was succeeded by his son Charles I. Name this English king who succeeded Elizabeth I in 1603 and founded the House of Stuart.

Alexander the Great ordered the rebuilding of the main temple of this city, Esagila. The Elamite King Shutruk-Nahunte put an end to its Kassite dynasty, and the Hittite king Murshili I deposed Samsu-Ditana, the last king of its first dynasty. The nearby city of Borsippa had a shrine to Nabu, the son of this city's chief god, Marduk. After the defeat of its army at Opis, Cyrus the Great took control of it without fighting, and Strabo attributes its eventual desertion to the founding of nearby Seleucia-Tigris. Identify this Mesopotamian city, ruled by Nebuchadnezzar and Hammurabi, and home to some nice hanging gardens.

Richard Olney used it to give the US authority to resolve a dispute over the Schomburgk Line, demanding arbitration to forestall a war. An even broader application was allowed in 1928 by the Clark Memorandum. George Canning had first proposed a joint British and American commitment, but John Quincy Adams encouraged solo action by its namesake. Eventually, FDR's Good Neighbor Policy overturned Theodore Roosevelt's corollary to this policy. Name this decree which states that the US will not allow European colonial powers to interfere in the Western Hemisphere, promulgated by the 5th President.

For a time, this country was governed by its original vice president, Santander. This country was created at the Congress of Angostura, and the Congress of Cúcuta created its constitution, which abolished the mita system of labor. Its final leader, Jose Domingo Caicedo, could not prevent José Antonio Páez from causing two countries to secede from it. Comprised of the territory of the former Spanish viceroyalty of New Granada, it included Panama, Ecuador, and Venezuela. Lasting from 1819 to 1830, name this short-lived republic led by Simon Bolivar, named for a modern-day country whose capital is Bogota.

The victory at this battle was greatly aided by John Honeyman, a spy who gave the opposing commander Johann Rall misleading information. The defenders surrendered in an orchard shortly after their commander was killed in the center of town, though the organized retreat maneuvers employed by those forces suggest popular accounts of their readiness were inaccurate. Along with Nathaniel Greene and John Sullivan, George Washington was able to secure victory against three regiments of Hessian mercenaries via a surprise attack after crossing the Delaware. Occurring on December 26th, 1776, identify this Revolutionary War victory for the Continental army that takes its name from the capital city of New Jersey.

Late in this man's life he agreed to retire to his farm at Ennery, while the Constitution he published proclaimed Catholicism as the state religion. He opted out of participating in Vincent Oge's early rebellion, and as a result of his switching of sides in the struggle for his country's independence, he was granted the post of Lieutenant Governor by Etienne Laveaux. This man had a falling out with the more radical Leger-Felicite Sothonax, and Gabriel Hedouville attempted to get him to take on the mulatto leader Andre Riguad which eventually happened in the War of the Knives. Identify this former slave who was responsible for liberating Haiti.

This man was threatened with war by the Austrian ambassador Hulsemann, and sent a ship to Istanbul to help Hungarian refugees. Andrew Jackson Donelson, nephew of the former president, was this man's running mate in one election and perhaps the greatest achievement during this man's presidency was the Treaty of Kanagawa. Gaining only Maryland's electoral vote in his first bid for election as president, this man's term saw the Fugitive Slave Act passed as part of the Compromise of 1850. Name this New York political figure, who succeeded to the presidency after the death of Zachary Taylor.

While fighting in the Siege of Veracruz, he met his future commander and earned two brevet promotions. His most notable accomplishments came after a defeat at Kernstown, which would be his only defeat in this campaign. He defeated Nathaniel Banks at Front Royal and John C. Fremont at Cross Keys, and harassed McDowell in the Valley Campaign. Name the general who was killed by friendly fire at the Battle of Chancellorsville and who, at the Battle of First Bull Run, received his memorable nickname.

A man named Juan Santos who claimed to be a descendent of this man took this man's name and led a rebellion in Tarma and Jauja in the 1740s. He was captured at Chillopampa but escaped and defeated his enemies at Chimborazo. This man sparred with his half-brother Huascar in a civil war after the death of his father Huayna Capac, and he was captured at the Battle of Cajamarca and ransomed for tons of gold and silver, but eventually suffocated and replaced by his brother, Tupac Huallpa. Name this man overthrown by Francisco Pizarro, an Incan emperor.

A comic strip-like work about the "Dream and Lie" of this man depicts a dead horse, a hairy heart, and lots of screaming women. This man's rise to power culminated after the assassination of Jose Calvo Sotelo, and he was preceded as ruler by Jose Primo de Rivera, the founder of his "Falange" (Fal-ON-hay) party. He sent the Blue Division to help Hitler during World War II, and Hitler sent the Condor Legion to help this man rise to power, leading to the bombing of the village of Guernica. Name this fascist Spanish dictator.
Francisco Paulino Hermenegildo Teodulo Franco y Bahamonde
